source: Ordinary brackets and standard deductions: Rev. Proc. 2024-40 inflation adjustments, with standard deduction amounts as adjusted by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA, P.L. 119-21) for TY2025. Social Security wage base: SSA 2025 announcement ($176,100; SSA press release Oct. 10, 2024 and Fact Sheet '2025 Social Security Changes'). Capital loss limit: IRC 1211(b) ($3,000; $1,500 if married filing separately), as applied on Schedule D line 21. Capital gain maximum zero rate / maximum 15 percent rate amounts (section 1(j)(5)(B)): Rev. Proc. 2024-40, section 3.03. Self-employment tax: rates per IRC 1401(a) (12.4% Social Security) and IRC 1401(b) (2.9% Medicare), applied on Schedule SE; net earnings from self-employment = 92.35% of Schedule C net profit per IRC 1402(a) as applied on Schedule SE line 4a; the deductible part of the SE tax is one-half per IRC 164(f) (Schedule SE line 13, to Schedule 1 line 15). Child tax credit, credit for other dependents, and additional child tax credit: Schedule 8812 (Form 1040) TY2025 and its instructions — CTC $2,200 per qualifying child (form line 5; the OBBBA increase is stated in the instructions' What's New), credit for other dependents $500 (form line 7), phaseout threshold $400,000 if married filing jointly and $200,000 for all other filing statuses (form line 9), with the excess over the threshold rounded up to the next multiple of $1,000 and multiplied by 5% (form lines 10-11); the nonrefundable credit is limited by Credit Limit Worksheet A in the Schedule 8812 instructions (Form 1040 line 18 minus other nonrefundable credits from Schedule 3); the additional child tax credit is capped at $1,700 per qualifying child (form line 16b; instructions' What's New) and at 15% of earned income over $2,500 (form Part II-A, lines 18a-20). Additional standard deduction for age 65 or blindness: Rev. Proc. 2024-40 and IR-2024-273 — the additional amount per condition (age 65 or older, or blind) is $1,600, increased to $2,000 if the individual is unmarried and not a surviving spouse; a taxpayer is considered 65 for TY2025 if born before January 2, 1961 (Instructions for Form 1040 (2025), Standard Deduction; the cutoff date is printed on the form itself, page 2, lines 12d/12e area: 'Were born before January 2, 1961'). Earned income credit: Rev. Proc. 2024-40, section 3.01 — phaseout threshold amounts $23,350 (one or more qualifying children) / $10,620 (no children) for all filing statuses except married filing jointly, $30,470 / $17,730 for MFJ; completed phaseout amounts $50,434 / $57,310 / $61,555 / $19,104 (one / two / three-or-more / no children) for all filing statuses except MFJ, $57,554 / $64,430 / $68,675 / $26,214 for MFJ; the credit is not allowed when aggregate investment income exceeds $11,950 (IRC 32(i), per Rev. Proc. 2024-40, section 3.01(2)). The no-children age test is 'at least age 25 but under age 65 at the end of 2025' (Instructions for Form 1040 (2025), line 27, Step 4: born after December 31, 1960, and before January 2, 2001; either spouse suffices on a joint return). The credit amounts themselves come from the TY2025 EIC Table (params/2025-eic-table.json).
